old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-cb10","title":"Python SlotClaim.decode_cose accepts reordered payload keys and trailing payload bytes (deterministic-CBOR parity gap vs Rust/C)","description":"Found during l2uk review (security pass, kimi-k3; verified against python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py). spec/decisions.jsonl slot-claim-cose-sign1 adjudicates the COSE payload as deterministic-CBOR. Rust from_cose now rejects non-ascending keys and trailing payload bytes (l2uk), and C rejects both implicitly (claim_compute_digest digests the received payload bytes, coap_slot_coord.c:394). Python decode_cose (slot_claim.py:198-233) uses cbor2.loads on the payload with no key-order check, no trailing-byte check, and no byte-equality re-encode gate; verify_slot_claim digests encode_claim_canonical(claim) (slot_claim.py:535), the canonical re-encode — exactly the pre-l2uk Rust behavior. Net: a relay can still flip Python vs {Rust,C} verdicts on a signature-valid claim with permuted keys or trailing payload bytes. Fix: in decode_cose, require payload keys strictly ascending (or byte-equality: encode_claim_canonical(decoded) == payload) and reject trailing payload bytes. Mitigating: l1qw.20 notes the Python wire receiver is currently missing, so live RF impact is deferred.
